newsitem.title: USA: Dlr/mark up sharply at US noon, hovers near highs.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/mark up sharply at US noon, hovers near highs.

text.p: Broad-based mark selling left the dollar sharply higher against the German currency at midsession following its mid-morning flight to 1.7732, a level not seen seen since August 1991.

The move came in tandem with the sterling's push beyond the psychologically important 3.00 barrier, fueled by market forecasts for tighter English monetary policy in the wake of a 25 basis point Bank of England rate hike on Thursday.
Both dollar/mark and sterling/mark tested their highs into midday. Dollar/mark was quoted at 1.7700/05. Sterling/mark was quoted at 2.9990/00 at 1230 EDT/1630 GMT.
Mark selling against the Italian lira, Swiss and French francs also fed the dollar trade, dealers said. Stop losses set just below 1.77 marks cemented dollar gains, they added.

"It's a pretty ugly day with a lot of mark selling in thin market conditions so prices moved very fast," said Ben Strauss, assistant vice president at Bank Julius Baer & Co. "Sterling/mark started it and then once we got through the 1.7570 level there were buy stops above there and then buy stops at the previous resistance."
Dollar/mark reportedly had a tight grip on 1.77 in the absence of any sterling/mark offers from the Bank of England.

Market talk suggested the Bank of England may come in with offers for sterling/mark at 3.00 in an effort to cull the sterling strength, but no signs of such a move were evident at midday, according to U.S. and European traders.

Longstanding concerns over the strength of the euro and signs the German economic recovery is lagging also weighed on the mark. Further, dealers were wary of Germany's Finance Minister's projection on Friday for a public sector deficit of 110 billion marks, or 3.0 percent of gross domestic product.
"A 3.0 percent deficit sounds a little optimistic," one dealer at a French bank said.
Dealers reported especially active dollar/mark and sterling/mark buying by funds.

Mark selling against the yen capped the dollar's move higher versus the yen, dealers said. Still, the dollar maintained a stronger bid to stay marginally higher at midday at 113.75/85 compared with 113.69/74 at the open.
Elsewhere, a drop of 0.1 percent in the June U.S. producer price index reported on Friday morning failed to elicit much response in the foreign exchange markets.

The dollar rose to 1.4590/00 Swiss francs at midday versus 1.4552/62 at the open. It was also stronger Canadian at 1.3703/08 against the open quote of 1.36997/02. Sterling fell to $1.6938/48 from $1.6980/90.
